q: What does the '0/1' in 0/1 knapsack mean?
options: Each item is either taken whole or left out
The bag is either full or empty
explain: Items cannot be split. If fractions were allowed, it would be the fractional knapsack, which greedy solves.

q: W = 50, items (weight, value) = (10, 60), (20, 100), (30, 120). What does greedy by value/weight give, and what is optimal?
explain: Greedy takes the ratios 6 and 5 first (weight 30, value 160); the third item no longer fits. Taking the second and third items gives 220.

q: What is the recurrence for K[i][c] when item i fits (wᵢ ≤ c)?
explain: Either skip item i, or take it and solve the rest with the remaining capacity using only the earlier items. Using K[i][c − wᵢ] would allow item i again (unbounded knapsack).

q: W = 7, items (1, 1), (3, 4), (4, 5), (5, 7). What is the best value?
explain: Items 2 and 3 weigh 3 + 4 = 7 and are worth 4 + 5 = 9. Greedy by ratio picks item 4 first and ends with only 8.

q: During the trace-back, how do you tell that item i was taken?
explain: If skipping item i gives the same value, the item is not needed. Otherwise it was taken, so subtract wᵢ from c.

q: What is the time complexity of the DP for n items and capacity W?
explain: There are (n + 1)(W + 1) cells, each filled in O(1).

q: Because it runs in Θ(n·W), the DP is a polynomial-time algorithm for 0/1 knapsack.
explain: False. W is written with about log W bits, so n·W can be exponential in the input size. The algorithm is pseudo-polynomial, and the problem is NP-complete.

q: In the one-row version, why must the capacity loop run from W down to wᵢ?
options: So each item is used at most once
explain: Going downwards, row[c − wᵢ] still holds the value from before item i was considered. Going upwards would let item i be added again.

q: Which problem is the special case of 0/1 knapsack where every value equals its weight?
explain: Maximising the total weight within W tells you whether some subset adds up to exactly W.

q: Greedy by value/weight is optimal for the fractional knapsack problem.
explain: True. With fractions allowed, filling the bag with the best ratio first, and taking part of the last item, is optimal (topic 23).
